author: yorickdowne
content:
That guide is a bit involved. I get it, you can innovate with a side car and you promote that. For most people, tbh, the TL;DR will be two parameters: `--builder-urls https://builder1.domain.xyz,https://builder2.domain2.xyz` and if trusted payments are desired, `--builder-max-execution-payment <amount>`. Exact parameter names client-specific, ofc. Lodestar for example also wants a parameter that says "I understand that trusted bids can be risky".

Client support for simple configuration via parameters is still evolving. I expect support in all clients Soon(tm). Lodestar, Prysm and Nimbus have full support now. Teku has full support under `-X` and will promote to "not experimental", probably Soon(tm). Lighthouse has a PR, in a release Soon(tm). Grandine is still working on a standalone VC and has parameters for ePBS in `develop`, in a release in time for Glamsterdam mainnet. Vero has parameters in a release candidate.

author: vladimir_ea
content: How do people discover what builder URLs are available? And shouldn’t the  max execution payment be configurable per builder? Some builders might be considered more trustworthy than others.

author: yorickdowne
content: I doubt that most users will reason about the exact max execution payment at all, much less by builder

author: yorickdowne
content:
They need to discover what URLs are available regardless, whether with commit boost or without. As the URL goes into the auth data.

One way to discover them is through <https://ethstaker.org/mev-relay-list>, which will be renamed to epbs-builder-list after the fork and currently holds both PBS and ePBS URLs

author: vladimir_ea
content: Why do you think that? Currently 90% of blocks are served by relays. Do you think users have no interest in distinguishing a well-established relay from a new unknown builder?

author: vladimir_ea
content: This of course means that 90% of blocks currently use trusted payments and no max is configured

author: yorickdowne
content: I think that only because I don't know how sophisticated the large staking outfits are. Moderately has been my impression so far, but that may have changed. Maybe they want to set by-builder trust limits. Which they can do via keymanager, via configuration file, or via a sidecar as well, for  sure

author: potuz
content: I think the default behavior should be to set this value to 0 or infty, you'd use infty for the trusted relays and zero for untrusted ones.

author: 0w3n6325
content: It probably should have been a bool. It'll be interesting to see on mainnet whether anyone actually set's a non-zero value less than 100 ETH. Like ether you trust the builder or you don't. And if you do and the bid is like 50 ETH wouldn't you want to risk missing the slot for a chance the receive 50 ETH?

author: potuz
content: yes, I believe at least for the first fork this will be even less than a bool, most operators would only contact directly really trusted builders so they'd take anything they give them. I do believe there will be endpoints relatively soon with new builders that can be contacted directly and those will not be trusted, so there I expect this to be essentially a bool (all or nothing). However,  the dial is not that much of a problem to have and it may have some actual applications: low volume apps that prepare their own blocks may want to keep a 1ETH funded builder and if they need to pay more to be included they can add a trustless part to their bid, operators may want to give them "some slack". At any rate, more options, even if not used don't really hurt here.

author: vladimir_ea
content: it is a slightly strange configuration; presumably no-one wants to set a cap on what they can actually be paid, this is more of a 'credible bid threshold'. Hard to see how you might arrive at a meaningful value for that - so, yes, would make more sense as a bool.

author: yorickdowne
content: I am going to set it to `65_536` and if anyone pays me that much, I'll be sending pictures from a sailboat

author: potuz
content: the cap is not in what they can be paid, the cap is on the trusted part of the payment. The builder is always allowed to send both values to be non-zero

author: potuz
content: it makes perfect sense for a validator to put there something like 0.1ETH meaning "for regular operations you can send me your usual blocks and not bother to add deposits, but if you ever send me a big bid, make sure to have the money on-chain".

author: vladimir_ea
content: for trustless payments builders need to deposit ETH on-chain - are they expected to deposit enough ETH to cover high value block payments? if the trusted payment component is set low, then the builder who wins a very high value blocks that pay the proposer multiple ETH will be the one with the largest trustless payment deposit.

author: vladimir_ea
content: and because those deposits must be made in advance, the builder must be well enough capitalised to put lots of idle ETH on chain.

author: vladimir_ea
content: (whereas with trusted payment the proposer can be paid from proceeds of the block itself)
